A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the degradation of the NSAIDs diclofenac (DCF) and piroxican (PRX) in the presence of a hydroxyl radical (OH*) is possible and the formation of new products was detected by RP-HPLCS.
the degradation of both diclofenic acid and piroxicams was found to be more pronounced in the presence of the hydroxyl radicals than in their absence.
diclofenac is more susceptible to hydroxyl radical oxidation/degradation than piroxicam.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of RP-HPLC is a useful method for studying the degradation/oxidation of NSAIDs in the presence of free radicals, and it could be a useful method for the analysis of the degradation/oxidative products formed in vivo.
the formation of degradation products is a complex process and the presence of OH radicals is only one of the possible causes.
the use of hydroxyl free radicals in combination with UV irradiation is an effective tool for the study of the degradation pathways of NSAIDs and other drugs.
